6º de Primaria · Inglés

Present simple and continuous

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

«I play football» y «I'm playing football» se traducen casi igual: «juego al fútbol» y «estoy jugando al fútbol». ¿Cuándo usarías cada una?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

«I play football» habla de algo que haces normalmente, por ejemplo todos los sábados. «I'm playing football» habla de algo que pasa ahora mismo, mientras lo dices. En inglés esta diferencia es muy importante.

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: Good morning from space!

Hi! My name is Ana and I'm an astronaut. Right now I am floating inside the International Space Station, about 400 kilometres above the Earth. I am writing this message on a tablet, and my pen is flying next to my head!

Life here is very different. We don't sleep in beds: we sleep in sleeping bags tied to the wall, so we don't float around at night. Every day we exercise for about two hours, because without gravity our muscles and bones get weak. We eat food from special packets, and we drink water that the station recycles again and again.

The station goes around the Earth very fast, so we see about sixteen sunrises and sixteen sunsets every day. It's amazing!

At the moment, my colleague Tom is doing an experiment with plants, and Yuki is talking to the control centre. And me? I am looking out of the window. I can see Spain, and the sun is shining on the sea. Bye for now!

1. Two presents

English has two present tenses. The present simple is for things we do often or things that are always true: «I walk to school every day», «Water boils at 100 °C». The present continuous is for things that are happening now: «Look! It's raining».

En castellano: el presente simple sirve para rutinas y verdades; el presente continuo, para lo que está pasando en este momento. En español también tenemos las dos formas («leo» y «estoy leyendo»), pero en inglés hay que elegir con más cuidado.

2. Present simple: affirmative

To make the present simple, use the verb without to: «I play», «you play», «we play», «they play». With he, she and it add -s: «she plays», «it rains».

Spelling (ortografía): verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x and -o add -es: watch → watches, go → goes, do → does. Consonant + y changes to -ies: study → studies, fly → flies. But vowel + y only adds -s: play → plays. Have is irregular: he has.

3. How do you say the -s?

In the present simple, the third person (he, she, it) ends in -s or -es. But this ending has three different sounds, like the -ed of the past:

  • /s/ after the sounds p, t, k, f: stops, gets, works, laughs. It sounds like the Spanish s.
  • /z/ after vowel sounds and most other consonants: plays, goes, reads, swims, lives. It sounds like a buzzing bee: «zzz».
  • /ɪz/ after the sounds s, z, sh, ch, x, and after ge, ce: watches, washes, kisses, fixes, dances, changes. Here the ending is a new syllable: «WAT-chiz», «DAN-siz».

Two verbs are special: does is pronounced «daz», not «dus», and says is pronounced «sez», not «seis».

Practise with this tongue twister: «She watches, washes and fixes the dishes, then she plays and sings and stops.» Clap once for each extra syllable /ɪz/!

Vídeo: Third Person Singular ✏️ GRAMMAR & SPELLING for Kids 🔡 Superlexia ⭐ Episode 19 · Smile and Learn - English (YouTube) · 81 mil visualizaciones

4. Present simple: negatives and questions

For negatives we use don't (do not) or doesn't (does not) + verb: «I don't like fish», «He doesn't like fish». Careful: after doesn't the verb has no -s.

For questions we put Do or Does first: «Do you like pizza?» – «Yes, I do. / No, I don't». «Does she speak French?» – «Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't». En castellano: en inglés la pregunta no se hace solo con la entonación, como en «¿te gusta la pizza?»; necesita el ayudante do/does.

5. Time words for the present simple

Some words tell us to use the present simple. They are frequency adverbs (adverbios de frecuencia): always, usually, often, sometimes, never. They go before the main verb but after the verb to be: «I usually have cereal», «She is always happy».

Other time expressions go at the end: every day, every Monday, on Saturdays, at the weekend, once a week. Example: «We go swimming twice a week». En castellano: «twice a week» es «dos veces por semana».

6. Present continuous: form

The present continuous has two parts: the verb to be (am / is / are) and the verb with -ing. «I am reading», «She is eating», «They are playing». In speaking we use short forms: I'm, she's, they're.

Spelling: verbs ending in -e lose the e: write → writing, dance → dancing. Short verbs ending in consonant + vowel + consonant double the last letter: swim → swimming, run → running, sit → sitting. Negative: «I'm not sleeping». Question: «Are you listening?» – «Yes, I am».

Vídeo: Present Continuous Verb Chant: What are you doing? · ELF Kids Videos (YouTube) · 2,8 millones de visualizaciones

7. Spelling the -ing form

Most verbs just add -ing: read → reading, play → playing, go → going. But there are some spelling rules:

  • Verbs ending in -e lose the e: make → making, write → writing, dance → dancing, ride → riding. But see → seeing (ee stays).
  • Verbs ending in -ie change to -y: lie → lying, die → dying, tie → tying.
  • Short verbs ending in one vowel + one consonant double the consonant: run → running, swim → swimming, sit → sitting, get → getting, stop → stopping, shop → shopping.
  • But we don't double w, x, y: snow → snowing, fix → fixing, play → playing.
  • Longer verbs double only if the last syllable is stressed: begin → beginning, but visit → visiting, listen → listening.

Tip: say the word aloud. In running or swimming, the vowel sound is short; the double consonant protects it. In riding or making, the vowel sound is long.

8. Time words for the present continuous

These words tell us that something is happening now: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, and also Look! and Listen! «Look! The baby is walking!», «Be quiet! Grandpa is sleeping».

We also use the present continuous for temporary things (cosas temporales): «I usually live in Madrid, but this month I'm staying with my aunt in Cádiz». En castellano: si algo pasa solo durante un tiempo, aunque no sea en este segundo exacto, también va en continuo.

9. Simple or continuous?

Compare: «My dad works in a hospital» (that is his job, always) and «My dad is working in the garden» (now, at this moment). «Sara speaks English» (she can, always) and «Sara is speaking English» (now, on the phone).

Some verbs are almost never in continuous: like, love, hate, want, know, understand, need. We say «I know the answer», not «I'm knowing». En castellano: son verbos de gustos, deseos y pensamientos; no son acciones que se ven, por eso van en simple.

10. Verbs we don't use in the continuous

Some verbs describe states (estados), not actions: feelings, thoughts, possession or senses. These state verbs are normally not used in the continuous, even when we talk about now:

  • Feelings: like, love, hate, want, need, prefer. «I want an ice cream now.» (not «I'm wanting»)
  • Thoughts: know, understand, believe, remember, think (= opinion). «I know the answer.» «I think it's a good idea.»
  • Possession: have (= own), belong, own. «This bag belongs to me.»
  • Senses: see, hear, smell, taste. «I hear music.»

Some of these verbs can be continuous when they mean an action:

  • «I have a dog» (possession) but «I'm having lunch» (action: comer).
  • «I think you're right» (opinion) but «I'm thinking about my holidays» (action: pensar en).

Remember the famous advert: «I'm lovin' it» is a play on words. In correct grammar, we say «I love it».

A good test: ask yourself if you can see the action happening, like a film. You can see someone eating, running or writing, so these verbs work in the continuous. But you can't see someone «knowing» or «belonging»: these are states inside the person or facts about the world, so we use the present simple. With this trick you will avoid one of the most common mistakes of students of English all over the world, such as «I am wanting» or «I am knowing».

Vídeo: State verbs - 6 Minute Grammar · BBC Learning English (YouTube) · 196 mil visualizaciones

11. Reading: a day at summer camp

Read Marta's message: «Hi Grandma! I'm at summer camp. Every day I get up at eight and I have breakfast with my friends. We usually go canoeing in the morning. I don't like the food very much, but the activities are fantastic! Right now I'm sitting by the lake and my friends are playing volleyball. The sun is shining. Love, Marta».

Find the two presents: the routine (get up, have, go, don't like) and the things happening now (am sitting, are playing, is shining).

12. Let's practise: picture game

Play in pairs. One student mimes an action (hace mímica) and the other asks: «Are you swimming?» – «No, I'm not». «Are you dancing?» – «Yes, I am!». Then change roles.

Second round: talk about your routine. «Do you walk to school?», «What time do you go to bed?», «How often do you play video games?». Answer with full sentences: «I sometimes play at the weekend». Consejo: escucha si la pregunta empieza por Are (ahora) o por Do (normalmente).

13. Present continuous for the future

The present continuous is not only for now. We also use it to talk about future plans that are already arranged (organizados): we know the time and the place, we have tickets or we have spoken to other people.

  • «I'm visiting my grandma on Saturday.»
  • «We're flying to London next week. We have the tickets!»
  • «What are you doing this weekend?» – «I'm playing in a basketball match.»
  • «She isn't coming to the party tomorrow.»

The important thing is the time expression: tomorrow, tonight, on Saturday, next week, this weekend, at five o'clock. Without it, the sentence talks about now. Compare: «I'm playing football» (ahora mismo) and «I'm playing football tomorrow» (un plan).

En castellano hacemos algo parecido con el presente: «Mañana voy al cine», «El sábado juego un partido».

A good place to see this tense is a diary or planner: «Monday: I'm having a piano lesson. Wednesday: we're going to the museum.»

14. School days around the world

Children all over the world go to school, but their days are not the same. Read and compare with your school:

  • In Japan, students clean their classrooms, corridors and toilets themselves at the end of the day. They say it teaches them to respect their school.
  • In Finland, children start compulsory school when they are seven years old, and they usually have a short break after each lesson.
  • In China, many schools do eye exercises every day: students massage the area around their eyes while music plays.
  • In some parts of the world, children walk for more than an hour to get to school, or travel by boat or even by cable car.
  • In Spain, most primary pupils have lunch at school and finish in the afternoon.

Now imagine you are a reporter. Write a short text about your school day with the present simple («We start at nine») and describe a photo of your class with the present continuous («Lucas is reading, the teacher is smiling»).

Vídeo: A look at « Journeys to school », around the world · UNESCO (YouTube) · 245 mil visualizaciones

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Complete with the present simple: «My brother (watch) ___ TV every evening.»

  1. My brother = he → hay que añadir -s.
  2. watch acaba en -ch → -es.

Resultado: My brother watches TV every evening.

Ejemplo 2. Complete with the present continuous: «Listen! The birds (sing) ___.»

  1. Listen! indica que pasa ahora → presente continuo.
  2. The birds = they → are.
  3. sing + -ing = singing.

Resultado: Listen! The birds are singing.

Ejemplo 3. Choose: «I (understand / am understanding) the question.»

  1. understand es un verbo de pensamiento.
  2. Estos verbos casi nunca van en continuo.

Resultado: I understand the question.

Ejemplo 4. How do you pronounce the -s in «dances»?

  1. The verb ends in the sound /s/ (ce).
  2. After s, z, sh, ch, x and ce, the ending is a new syllable.

Resultado: /ɪz/: «DAN-siz».

Ejemplo 5. Correct: «I'm knowing the answer.»

  1. Know is a state verb (thought).
  2. State verbs are not normally continuous.

Resultado: I know the answer.

Errores típicos

  • Olvidar la -s con he/she/it: «she play» → «she plays».
  • Poner -s después de doesn't: «he doesn't likes» → «he doesn't like».
  • Olvidar el verbo to be en el continuo: «I reading» → «I'm reading».
  • No doblar la consonante: «swiming», «runing» → «swimming», «running».
  • Usar el continuo con like, want o know: «I'm wanting» → «I want».
  • Decir «I'm wanting» o «I'm knowing»: los verbos de estado no van en continuo.
  • Escribir «runing» o «makeing»: hay que doblar la consonante o quitar la e.

PracticaResponde sin mirar arriba. Equivocarse aquí también enseña.

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Write the he/she form: go, fly, wash, have.

    Ver solución
    goes, flies, washes, has.

  2. Write the -ing form: write, swim, play, sit.

    Ver solución
    writing, swimming, playing, sitting.

  3. Make it negative: «Tom likes carrots.»

    Ver solución
    Tom doesn't like carrots.

  4. Write the -ing form: swim, make, play, lie.

    Ver solución
    swimming, making, playing, lying.

  5. Which sound? works, plays, watches.

    Ver solución
    /s/, /z/, /ɪz/.

  6. Choose: «I (want / am wanting) a drink.»

    Ver solución
    want.

  7. Complete: «We ___ (visit) Grandma tomorrow.»

    Ver solución
    are visiting.

  8. Where do students clean their classrooms?

    Ver solución
    In Japan.

Nivel medio

  1. Make a question: «They live in Seville.»

    Ver solución
    Do they live in Seville?

  2. Complete: «Look! The cat (climb) ___ the tree.»

    Ver solución
    is climbing.

  3. Complete: «We (have) ___ English on Mondays.»

    Ver solución
    have.

  4. Put the adverb in the right place: «I am late. (never)»

    Ver solución
    I am never late.

  5. Correct the mistake: «She is knowing the answer.»

    Ver solución
    She knows the answer.

  6. Write the -ing form: sit, write, begin, visit.

    Ver solución
    sitting, writing, beginning, visiting.

  7. Correct: «This book is belonging to me.»

    Ver solución
    This book belongs to me.

  8. Explain the difference: «I have a cat» / «I'm having breakfast».

    Ver solución
    Have = possession (state); having = action (eating).

  9. Write three arranged plans for next weekend.

    Ver solución
    Open answer. Example: I'm playing tennis on Saturday.

  10. How many sunrises do astronauts see every day on the ISS?

    Ver solución
    About sixteen.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Translate: «Normalmente voy en bici, pero hoy estoy caminando.»

    Ver solución
    I usually go by bike, but today I'm walking.

  2. Write two sentences about you: one routine and one thing you are doing now.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I play basketball on Tuesdays. Now I'm doing my English homework.

  3. Write a tongue twister with verbs in /ɪz/.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  4. Why do we write «running» with double n but «raining» with one n?

    Ver solución
    Run has one vowel + one consonant; rain has two vowels.

  5. Write a dialogue: «What are you doing this weekend?» with three plans.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  6. Write a short report about your school day (present simple) and a photo description (present continuous).

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeA day in our school

La clase prepara un vídeo en inglés para enseñar su colegio a una escuela de otro país.

Pasos

  1. Escribid el guion de un día típico con el present simple.
  2. Grabad escenas y describid lo que está pasando con el present continuous.
  3. Añadid los planes de la clase para la semana siguiente con el present continuous de futuro.
  4. Revisad la pronunciación de -s y -ing y compartid el vídeo con una escuela amiga, por ejemplo por eTwinning.

Producto final: Un vídeo en inglés sobre la vida en el colegio.

Cómo se valora

  • Uses present simple for routines.
  • Uses present continuous for now and for plans.
  • Pronounces the -s endings correctly.
  • Speaks clearly and with confidence.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Durante la cena, preguntad en inglés «What are you doing?» y «What do you do on Saturdays?» y comparad las respuestas.
  • Narrad en voz alta lo que hace alguien en un vídeo sin sonido: «He's running, he's jumping…».
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Comunicación oral y escrita sobre rutinas, hábitos y acciones en curso; presente simple y continuo (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Mímica por parejas con preguntas Are you…?
  • Encuesta de rutinas de la clase con How often do you…? y gráfico de resultados.
  • Describir una foto del patio en presente continuo.

Revisado el 22 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Use the present simple for habits and facts (hábitos y verdades)
  • Use the present continuous for actions happening now (ahora mismo)
  • Make negatives and questions with do/does and am/is/are
  • Choose the right tense with time words: every day, now, at the moment
  • Pronounce the -s of the third person correctly
  • Spell the -ing form without mistakes
  • Know which verbs are not used in the continuous
  • Use the present continuous for future plans

Palabras clave

present simple · present continuous · -s / -es / -ies · do / does · don't / doesn't · am / is / are + -ing · every day · now · at the moment

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
